en router.explanation: "En router" means "a router". To tell someone what to try when the internet stops working: "Prøv at genstarte routeren" (Try restarting the router).

en rude.explanation: "En rude" means "a window pane". To talk about the whole window, not just the glass, use "et vindue" (a window): "Vinduet er åbent" (The window is open).

en rullepølse.explanation: "En rullepølse" means "a rolled pork sausage". It is built from "rulle" (roll) and "pølse" (sausage), but it is not cooked: it is spiced pork that is sliced thin and eaten cold on bread.

en rulletrappe.explanation: "En rulletrappe" means "an escalator". It is built from "at rulle" (to roll) and "en trappe" (a staircase). The same "rulle" is in "en rullestol" (a wheelchair).

en runde.explanation: "En runde" means "a round", as in one turn in a game. To say you take a short walk: "Vi går en runde i parken" (We take a stroll in the park). To say you buy drinks for everyone: "Jeg giver en runde" (I am buying a round).

en rundkørsel.explanation: "En rundkørsel" means "a roundabout". It is built from "rund" (round) and "kørsel" (driving). Danish traffic goes counterclockwise around it. To tell someone which way to leave it: "Tag anden afkørsel i rundkørslen" (Take the second exit at the roundabout).

en rundvisning.explanation: "En rundvisning" means "a guided tour". It is built from "rund" (round) and "visning" (a showing). To ask for one: "Kan vi få en rundvisning?" (Can we get a tour?)

en rune.explanation: "En rune" means "a rune". A stone with runes cut into it is "en runesten" (a rune stone). The Jelling stones in Denmark are rune stones.

en russer.explanation: "En russer" means "a Russian". It comes from "Rusland" (Russia). To say a person is Russian: "Min nabo er russer" (My neighbor is Russian). For the language, use "russisk" (Russian): "Hun taler russisk" (She speaks Russian).

en rute.explanation: "En rute" means "a route". To say where a bus goes: "Bussen kører på en fast rute gennem byen" (The bus runs on a fixed route through town).

en rutine.explanation: "En rutine" means "a routine". It also means experience from doing something many times. To say someone is experienced: "Hun har stor rutine" (She has a lot of experience).

en rutsjebane.explanation: "En rutsjebane" means "a slide, a roller coaster". To talk about the slide at a playground: "Børnene leger på rutsjebanen" (The children play on the slide). To talk about the ride at an amusement park: "Rutsjebanen i forlystelsesparken er hurtig" (The roller coaster at the amusement park is fast).

en ryg.explanation: "En ryg" means "a back", as in the body part. To say your back hurts: "Jeg har ondt i ryggen" (My back hurts), literally "I have pain in the back". To say you lie face up: "Jeg ligger på ryggen" (I am lying on my back).

en rygrad.explanation: "En rygrad" means "a spine", as in the bones of the back. To say a person has courage, use "rygrad" the way English uses "backbone": "Hun har rygrad" (She has backbone).

en rygsæk.explanation: "En rygsæk" means "a backpack". It is built from "ryg" (back) and "sæk" (sack). To say you put it on: "Jeg tager rygsækken på" (I put on the backpack).

en rynke.explanation: "En rynke" means "a wrinkle". The same word is in a verb phrase. To say someone frowns: "Han rynker panden" (He frowns), literally "He wrinkles the forehead".

en rysten.explanation: "En rysten" means "a shiver". It comes from the verb "at ryste" (to shake). To say you shake from the cold: "Jeg ryster af kulde" (I am shaking from the cold).

en rytme.explanation: "En rytme" means "a rhythm". To talk about the pattern of a day: "dagens rytme" (the rhythm of the day). To tell someone to keep the beat: "Hold rytmen" (Keep the rhythm).

en rådgiver.explanation: "En rådgiver" means "an adviser". It is built from "råd" (advice) and "giver" (giver). To name a money adviser: "en økonomisk rådgiver" (a financial adviser).

en række.explanation: "En række" means "a row". To talk about several rows: "rækker af stole" (rows of chairs). To say a number of things, use "en række" before the plural: "en række problemer" (a number of problems).

en rækkevidde.explanation: "En rækkevidde" means "a range / reach". It is built from "række" (reach) and "vidde" (width). To talk about how far an electric car can go: "elbilens rækkevidde" (the electric car's range). For something kept where children cannot get it: "uden for børns rækkevidde" (out of children's reach).

en ræv.explanation: "En ræv" means "a fox". To say someone is cunning: "Han er så snu som en ræv" (He is as sly as a fox).

en rødbede.explanation: "En rødbede" means "a beet". The name starts with "rød" (red). To say pickled beets: "syltede rødbeder" (pickled beets).

en rødmen.explanation: "En rødmen" means "a blush". For the action, use the verb "at rødme" (to blush): "Hun rødmer, når han ser på hende" (She blushes when he looks at her).

en rødspætte.explanation: "En rødspætte" means "a plaice". The name starts with "rød" (red), for the orange-red spots on the fish. In Denmark, fried plaice is a traditional dish.

en rødvin.explanation: "En rødvin" means "a red wine". It is built from "rød" (red) and "vin" (wine). To say a glass of it, Danish has no word for "of": "et glas rødvin" (a glass of red wine).

en røgalarm.explanation: "En røgalarm" means "a smoke alarm". It is built from "røg" (smoke) and "alarm" (alarm). To say it needs a new battery: "Røgalarmen skal have nyt batteri" (The smoke alarm needs a new battery).

en røremaskine.explanation: "En røremaskine" means "a stand mixer". It is built from "at røre" (to stir) and "en maskine" (a machine). To say you whip cream with it: "Jeg pisker fløde i røremaskinen" (I whip cream in the stand mixer).

en røver.explanation: "En røver" means "a robber", a person who uses force or threats. Do not mix it up with "en tyv" (a thief), who steals without force: "Tyven tog min cykel" (The thief took my bike).

et rat.explanation: "Et rat" means "a steering wheel". Do not mix it up with "et hjul" (a wheel that rolls on the ground): "Bilen har fire hjul" (The car has four wheels).

et realkreditlån.explanation: "Et realkreditlån" means "a mortgage". It is built from "realkredit" (mortgage credit) and "et lån" (a loan). In Denmark, the loan comes from "et realkreditinstitut" (a mortgage credit institution). To say you take one out: "Vi optager et realkreditlån" (We are taking out a mortgage).

et reb.explanation: "Et reb" means "a rope". A thinner cord is "en snor" (a string): "Hun bandt pakken med en snor" (She tied the package with a string). To say you skip rope: "Børnene hopper i reb" (The children are skipping rope).

et referat.explanation: "Et referat" means "a summary". For a meeting, it is the written minutes. To say you write them: "at skrive referat" (to write the minutes). The word comes from the verb "at referere" (to report).

et regeringsparti.explanation: "Et regeringsparti" means "a governing party". It is built from "regering" (government) and "parti" (party). To name a party outside the government: "Et oppositionsparti kritiserer regeringen" (An opposition party criticizes the government).

et regnskab.explanation: "Et regnskab" means "accounts". To say someone does a company's accounts: "Han laver regnskab for firmaet" (He does the accounts for the company). The accounts for a whole year are "et årsregnskab" (annual accounts).

et rejsebureau.explanation: "Et rejsebureau" means "a travel agency". It is built from "rejse" (trip) and "bureau" (office). To say you will phone one: "Jeg ringer til rejsebureauet" (I will call the travel agency).

et rejsekort.explanation: "Et rejsekort" means "a travel card". In Denmark, it is the card for buses, trains and the metro. To remind someone to tap out when they get off: "Husk at checke ud" (Remember to check out).

et rejsemål.explanation: "Et rejsemål" means "a destination". It is built from "rejse" (trip) and "mål" (goal). To ask where someone is going: "Hvad er jeres rejsemål?" (What is your destination?)

et rektangel.explanation: "Et rektangel" means "a rectangle". The spelling differs from English: Danish has "k" where English has "c", and ends in "gel". The "e" drops when the word grows, as in "rektanglet" (the rectangle) and "rektangler" (rectangles).

et rengøringsmiddel.explanation: "Et rengøringsmiddel" means "a cleaning product". It is built from "rengøring" (cleaning) and "et middel" (a product). To ask in a shop: "Hvor er rengøringsmidlerne?" (Where are the cleaning products?)

et renseri.explanation: "Et renseri" means "a dry cleaner's". It comes from the verb "at rense" (to clean). To say you take a coat there: "Jeg afleverer jakken på renseriet" (I drop the jacket off at the dry cleaner's).

et repertoire.explanation: "Et repertoire" means "a repertoire". To say what music a singer can perform: "Hendes repertoire omfatter både jazz og blues" (Her repertoire includes both jazz and blues).

et resultat.explanation: "Et resultat" means "a result". To say the score of a match: "Resultatet blev 2-1" (The result was 2-1).

et resumé.explanation: "Et resumé" means "a summary". Do not use it for a job application. For that, Danish uses the short word "CV" (a résumé): "Send dit CV" (Send your résumé).

et ribben.explanation: "Et ribben" means "a rib". It is also in "ribbensteg" (roast pork with crackling), built from "ribben" and "en steg" (a roast). Roast pork with crackling is a traditional Danish Christmas dish.

et ritual.explanation: "Et ritual" means "a ritual". To say a daily habit is a ritual for you: "Morgenkaffen er et ritual for mig" (The morning coffee is a ritual for me).

et rivejern.explanation: "Et rivejern" means "a grater". It is built from "at rive" (to grate) and "jern" (iron). To say you grate cheese: "Jeg river osten" (I grate the cheese).

et rovdyr.explanation: "Et rovdyr" means "a predator". It is built from "rov" (loot) and "dyr" (animal). The same "rov" is in "en rovfugl" (a bird of prey).

et rum.explanation: "Et rum" means "a room / space". To talk about outer space, use "verdensrummet" (outer space). To say there is room for someone, use "plads" (room) instead: "Der er plads til os" (There is room for us).

et rumfang.explanation: "Et rumfang" means "a volume", as in the amount of space. For how loud a sound is, use "lydstyrke" (loudness) instead: "Skru lydstyrken op" (Turn the volume up).

et rumskib.explanation: "Et rumskib" means "a spaceship". It is built from "rum" (space) and "et skib" (a ship). To say a spaceship takes off: "Rumskibet letter" (The spaceship takes off).

et rumvæsen.explanation: "Et rumvæsen" means "an alien". It is built from "rum" (space) and "et væsen" (a being). To ask what someone believes: "Tror du på rumvæsener?" (Do you believe in aliens?)

et rundstykke.explanation: "Et rundstykke" means "a bread roll". It is built from "rund" (round) and "et stykke" (a piece). To order at a bakery: "Jeg vil gerne have to rundstykker" (I would like two rolls).

et ry.explanation: "Et ry" means "a reputation". To say someone is known for something: "Han har ry for at være stædig" (He has a reputation for being stubborn).

et rygte.explanation: "Et rygte" means "a rumor". To say people are talking about something: "Der går et rygte om, at butikken lukker" (There is a rumor that the store is closing).

et råd.explanation: "Et råd" means "a piece of advice". The same word is in the phrase "at have råd til" (to be able to afford). To say you cannot afford something, use "råd" without "et": "Jeg har ikke råd til det" (I cannot afford it).

et rådhus.explanation: "Et rådhus" means "a town hall". It is built from "råd" (council) and "et hus" (a house). In Copenhagen, "Københavns Rådhus" (Copenhagen City Hall) stands on "Rådhuspladsen" (City Hall Square).

et rådyr.explanation: "Et rådyr" means "a roe deer". The ending is "dyr" (animal), as in "et rovdyr" (a predator). In Denmark, the roe deer is the smallest wild deer.

et rækkehus.explanation: "Et rækkehus" means "a townhouse". It is built from "række" (row) and "hus" (house). To say where you live: "Vi bor i rækkehus" (We live in a townhouse).

et røntgenbillede.explanation: "Et røntgenbillede" means "an X-ray image". It is built from "røntgen", named after the German scientist Wilhelm Röntgen, who discovered X-rays, and "et billede" (a picture). To say a doctor takes one: "Lægen tager et røntgenbillede af min arm" (The doctor takes an X-ray of my arm).

et rør.explanation: "Et rør" means "a pipe". To say the water pipe has burst: "Røret er sprunget" (The pipe has burst).

et røveri.explanation: "Et røveri" means "a robbery". It comes from "en røver" (a robber). To say someone committed one: "Han begik et røveri" (He committed a robbery).

radikal.explanation: "Radikal" means "radical". To say a change for the better is big: "en radikal forbedring" (a radical improvement). In Denmark, "Radikale Venstre" is the name of a political party.

raps.explanation: "En raps" means "rapeseed". To say rapeseed grows somewhere, leave out "en": "Der gror raps på marken" (Rapeseed is growing in the field).

rar.explanation: "Rar" means "nice". To say you are glad to meet someone: "Rart at møde dig" (Nice to meet you). To say a moment was pleasant: "Det var rart at se dig" (It was nice to see you).

rasende.explanation: "Rasende" means "furious". It comes from the verb "at rase" (to rage). For light annoyance, use "irriteret" (annoyed): "Jeg er irriteret" (I am annoyed).

rask.explanation: "Rask" means "healthy", as in not ill. To say you get well after an illness: "at blive rask" (to get well). For food or habits that are good for you, use "sund" (healthy): "Frugt er sundt" (Fruit is healthy).

rastløs.explanation: "Rastløs" means "restless". It is built from "en rast" (a break) and "-løs" (without), so it is literally "without a break". To say how you feel: "Jeg føler mig rastløs" (I feel restless).

rationel.explanation: "Rationel" means "rational". To say a method is efficient: "en rationel arbejdsgang" (an efficient way of working).

rav.explanation: "Et rav" means "amber". To say what something is made of: "Ringen er lavet af rav" (The ring is made of amber).

realistisk.explanation: "Realistisk" means "realistic". English ends in "-ic", but Danish ends in "-isk". To say a film looks like real life: "Filmen er meget realistisk" (The film is very realistic).

regelmæssigt.explanation: "Regelmæssigt" means "regularly". It comes from "en regel" (a rule). To say you do something at steady times: "Jeg ringer regelmæssigt til min mor" (I call my mother regularly). Do not mix it up with "ofte" (often), which gives no steady pattern: "Jeg træner ofte, men ikke hver mandag" (I exercise often, but not every Monday).

registreret.explanation: "Registreret" means "registered". It comes from the verb "at registrere" (to register). For registered mail, Danish uses "anbefalet" (recommended): "et anbefalet brev" (a registered letter).

regn.explanation: "Regn" means "rain". To say it is raining, use the verb: "Det regner" (It is raining). Danish does not say "Det er regn".

regnfuld.explanation: "Regnfuld" means "rainy". It is built from "regn" (rain) and "-fuld" (full of), as in "fredfuld" (peaceful). To say a week was rainy: "Det har været en regnfuld uge" (It has been a rainy week).

regnfuldt.explanation: "Regnfuldt" means "rainy". It is built from "regn" (rain) and "-fuldt" (full of). To say it is raining right now, use the verb: "Det regner" (It is raining).

regntøj.explanation: "Regntøj" means "rain gear". It is built from "regn" (rain) and "tøj" (clothes). This word has no article, so you say it without "et": "Tag regntøj på" (Put on rain gear).

regnvejr.explanation: "Regnvejr" means "rainy weather". It is built from "regn" (rain) and "vejr" (weather). To say rain is falling right now, use the verb: "Det regner" (It is raining).

rejer.explanation: "Rejer" means "shrimp". It is the plural of "en reje" (a shrimp). To say a sandwich with shrimp: "en rejemad" (a shrimp sandwich), built from "reje" and "mad" (food).

relativt.explanation: "Relativt" means "relatively". It is weaker than "meget" (very): "relativt dyr" (relatively expensive) says less than "meget dyr" (very expensive).

relevant.explanation: "Relevant" means "relevant". To say something does not matter for the topic: "Det er ikke relevant" (That is not relevant).

religiøs.explanation: "Religiøs" means "religious". It comes from "en religion" (a religion). To say a person has faith, you can also use "troende" (a believer): "Hun er troende" (She is a believer).

remoulade.explanation: "En remoulade" means "a remoulade". In Denmark, it is served with fried fish and on hot dogs.

ren.explanation: "Ren" means "clean". It also means "pure": "rent vand" (pure water). To say you clean a room, use "at gøre rent" (to clean): "Jeg gør rent i stuen" (I clean the living room).

reserveret.explanation: "Reserveret" means "reserved". It comes from the verb "at reservere" (to reserve). To say a person is shy and keeps their distance: "Han er lidt reserveret" (He is a bit reserved).

respekt.explanation: "Respekt" means "respect". Danish spells the ending "kt", where English has "ct". To say you respect your boss: "Han har stor respekt for sin chef" (He has great respect for his boss).

resten.explanation: "Resten" means "the rest". To say you will do the remaining part later: "Jeg tager resten i morgen" (I will take the rest tomorrow). Do not mix it up with "rester" (leftovers): "Vi spiser rester" (We eat leftovers).

rester.explanation: "Rester" means "leftovers". For one small bit that remains, use "en rest" (a leftover): "Der er en rest af kagen" (There is a bit of the cake left).

retfærdig.explanation: "Retfærdig" means "fair". The opposite is "uretfærdig" (unfair): "Det er uretfærdigt" (That is unfair). Danish also borrows the English word "fair": "Det er ikke fair" (That is not fair).

retfærdighed.explanation: "En retfærdighed" means "justice". To talk about justice in general, leave out "en": "Der skal være retfærdighed" (There must be justice). The matching word for a decision is "retfærdig" (fair): "en retfærdig dom" (a fair verdict).

retskrivning.explanation: "En retskrivning" means "spelling rules". It is built from "ret" (correct) and "skrivning" (writing). In Denmark, the official spelling rules are in "Retskrivningsordbogen" (the spelling dictionary).

retssikkerhed.explanation: "En retssikkerhed" means "a legal certainty". It is built from "rets" (of the law) and "sikkerhed" (security). To say a reform makes people safer under the law: "Reformen styrker retssikkerheden" (The reform strengthens legal certainty).

related.en: a state under the rule of law

ridning.explanation: "Ridning" means "horse riding". It comes from the verb "at ride" (to ride). To say you went on one outing: "Vi tog på en ridetur" (We went on a ride).

rig.explanation: "Rig" means "rich". To say someone has a lot of something other than money: "rig på erfaring" (rich in experience). Do not mix it up with "et rige" (a kingdom): "Kongen styrer et stort rige" (The king rules a large kingdom).

rigdom.explanation: "En rigdom" means "a wealth". To say there are many details: "en rigdom af detaljer" (a wealth of details).

rigeligt.explanation: "Rigeligt" means "plenty". To politely turn down more: "Mere kaffe?" "Nej tak, jeg har rigeligt." (More coffee? No thanks, I have plenty.)

rigtig.explanation: "Rigtig" means "real". To say something is correct: "det rigtige svar" (the right answer). Before another describing word it means "really": "rigtig god" (really good).

rimelig.explanation: "Rimelig" means "reasonable". To say you do not think something is fair: "Det er ikke rimeligt" (That is not reasonable).

ris.explanation: "Ris" means "rice". At Christmas in Denmark, the dessert "risalamande" (rice pudding with almonds) is made with rice.

risengrød.explanation: "En risengrød" means "a rice porridge". It is built from "ris" (rice) and "en grød" (a porridge). The cold Christmas dessert made from it is "risalamande" (rice pudding with almonds): "Til jul får vi risalamande" (At Christmas we have risalamande).
